notes.ios:
ReFineID is a smart-card driver. It makes the certificates on a Finnish identity card (FINEID) available to the operating system, so Safari can use them to sign in to Finnish public e-services at suomi.fi, the government's national service portal.

There is no account to demonstrate. The app has no login, no server, no registration, and collects no data. Nothing in it sits behind credentials, so there is no user name and password we can supply: none exists.

What the app needs is the card itself. The identity card is a legal identity document issued by the Finnish Police to one named citizen, in the same category as a passport; the certificates on it are issued by the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency. It cannot be duplicated, transferred, or issued for testing, so we are unable to put one in the reviewer's hands.

DEMONSTRATION MODE

This build carries one, added in answer to the previous review. To use it:

1. Press and hold the ReFineID icon on the Home Screen.
2. Choose "Demo Mode".
3. Type any digits as the card access number and any digits as the basic code, then tap "Read Certificate from Card".
4. On iPhone the system scan sheet opens and closes on its own; an iPad has no NFC antenna, so it pauses for the same moment without a sheet. The screen then names a test person, DOE JANE 12345678N.

"Demo Mode" is shown at the bottom of the screen for as long as the mode is on. It lasts one launch: only the Home Screen action turns it on, so no ordinary launch can enter it, and quitting the app ends it.

Nothing in demonstration mode touches a card or the system. No certificate is read, nothing is stored, no token is registered, and the digits typed into the two fields are not saved. The test person is a name and not a certificate, so the system is offered no identity: there is none to offer. What is demonstrated is the flow, which is the same screens and the same scan sheet a card goes through.

Also verifiable without a card:
- Every screen is available in English, Finnish and Swedish, and with VoiceOver, larger text, and the dark interface. The test person is named in each language.
- The camera button beside the card access number opens a scanner for the QR code printed on the card.

This build reads the card and publishes its certificate to the system. It does not sign documents; that is the Mac app.
The complete source is public at https://github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple, including the card protocol and this demonstration mode, so the behaviour behind the card can be read directly.
notes.macos:
ReFineID is a smart-card driver. It makes the certificates on a Finnish identity card (FINEID) available to the operating system, so Safari can use them to sign in to Finnish public e-services at suomi.fi, the government's national service portal.

There is no account to demonstrate. The app has no login, no server, no registration, and collects no data. Nothing in it sits behind credentials, so there is no user name and password we can supply: none exists.

What the app needs is the card itself. The identity card is a legal identity document issued by the Finnish Police to one named citizen, in the same category as a passport; the certificates on it are issued by the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency. It cannot be duplicated, transferred, or issued for testing, so we are unable to put one in the reviewer's hands.

Verifiable without a card, on this build:
- The app launches and reports "Present your identity card to the reader" rather than failing.
- The bundled CryptoTokenKit token extension registers with the system on first launch and appears in the smart-card system's driver list with no card present. That registration is the product's whole purpose.
- Settings contains the PIN pane, which shows the card's change and reset tasks and its attempt counters, and the time-stamp authority list used when signing a document.
- Every screen is available in English, Finnish and Swedish, and with VoiceOver, larger text, and the dark interface.

The app makes outbound connections for one purpose: an archival signature fetches a qualified time stamp and the revocation data proving its chain. It binds no listening socket.
The complete source is public at https://github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple, including the card protocol, so the behaviour behind the card can be read directly.

If a demonstration mode is the expected remedy for an app whose hardware is a personal identity document, please say so and we will add one.

description.macos:
A reader for the Finnish identity card.

Insert your identity card into a USB smart-card reader and sign in to e-services directly in Safari with the certificate on your card. Drop a PDF on ReFineID to sign it with a qualified signature.

ReFineID is open source: github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple
description.ios:
ReFineID brings the Finnish identity card to iPhone and iPad.

Read your card with a USB-C smart-card reader, or wirelessly on iPhone, then sign in to e-services directly in Safari with the certificate on your card.

ReFineID is open source: github.com/ReFineID/ReFineID-Apple
